newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rican leader to travel to Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rican leader to travel to Taiwan.

text.p: Costa Rican President Jose Maria Figueres on Tuesday begins an Asian trip that will include a stay in Taiwan, a country that Central American countries have backed despite threats from China.

Figueres was due to arrive in Taipei on Aug. 9 after a visit to Malaysia and will return on Aug. 14, a statement from the president's office said on Monday. He was seeking technological, educational and financial support.
His visit to Taiwan will closely follow that of Nicaraguan leader Arnoldo Aleman, who left Managua on a five-day visit to Taipei on Sunday.

Central American nations have courted Taiwan as a badly needed source of foreign investment, and Taiwan in turn has welcomed their diplomatic support amid growing efforts by Beijing to isolate it internationally.
Costa Rica, Nicaragua and a handful of other countries recently proposed that the U.N. General Assembly open discussions when it meets in September granting membership to Taiwan.
China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province, opposed the move and has made unspecified threats against Nicaragua and the other countries that backed U.N. membership for Taiwan.

On Monday the Taipei government announced President Lee Teng-hui would visit the Central American countries of El Salvador and Panama in September. That trip, which will include a stopover in Hawaii, will be Lee's first time abroad since 1995, when he visited the United States and aroused the wrath of China.
